AudioGraphOptions.latencyHint: Passed to `new AudioContext({ latencyHint })`, a browser buffer-size preference with no native audio-session equivalent that means the same thing on every platform.
AudioGraphOptions.smoothing: Sets an AnalyserNode's smoothingTimeConstant. Native has no single shared analyser AudioGraphPlugin owns — SpectrumPlugin and PcmEqualiser each keep their own SpectrumHistory, the same architecture split AudioGraphPlugin.context already carries.
AudioGraphPlugin.analyserSource: Returns an AnalyserNode. The native equivalent is the frame tap, which pushes frames rather than handing out a node to read.
AudioGraphPlugin.context: The Web Audio AudioContext itself. Native processing goes through the AudioDspGraph port, which is a different object with a different lifetime.
AudioGraphPlugin.insertEffect: Takes and returns AudioNode. Inserting arbitrary nodes into a chain is a Web Audio capability with no native counterpart.
AudioGraphPlugin.outputNode: Returns an AudioNode. There is no node graph natively; AudioDspGraph is a fixed EQ and tap interface.
AudioGraphPlugin.post: Takes and returns AudioNode. See insertEffect.
AudioGraphPlugin.pre: Takes and returns AudioNode. See insertEffect.
CanvasOptions.pointerEvents: The CSS pointer-events property on the canvas element. Compose decides hit testing per node, not with a stylesheet value.
CanvasPlugin.canvas: Returns the HTMLCanvasElement. The native plugin owns a surface the host mounts, not an element.
CanvasPlugin.context: Returns a CanvasRenderingContext2D. Native renderers draw through the toolkit's own scope.
CastSenderPlugin.connect: Opens the browser's Cast session picker and throws when the Cast SDK is absent from the page. No native platform offers a picker to open; a native app shows its own device list and calls transfer(target, item, position).
DesktopUiButtonOptions.chapterNext: Split from chapterPrev so a consumer can show one without the other. ChromeButtons.chapters is one flag gating both directions together; independent toggling isn't offered.
DesktopUiButtonOptions.chapterPrev: See chapterNext — the same single ChromeButtons.chapters flag.
DrmPlugin.mediaKeys: Returns the browser's MediaKeys off the video element. No native counterpart.
EmbedOptions.applyIframeTweaks: Rewrites attributes on an iframe. There is no iframe outside a browser.
KeyHandlerPlugin.scope: Returns the EventTarget the keydown listener attaches to. Natively the platform delivers key events; nothing is attached to a node.
MessageOptions.mountSelector: A CSS selector naming the DOM node to mount into. Compose has no selector and no document; the counterpart is the slot the host passes.
OctopusOptions.legacyWorkerUrl: The URL of a JavaScript worker for browsers without WebAssembly threads. The port links libass directly.
ScrobbleOptions.scrobbler: Injected through ScrobblePlugin's own constructor (`private val scrobbler: Scrobbler = NoopScrobbler`) rather than an options data class field, the same swap point the web's opts.scrobbler is — a private constructor parameter carries no public ABI signature for this tool to find under any name.
OctopusOptions.lazyFileLoading: Chunked loading for a JS Worker's own file handling. AssRenderer.loadTrack takes the whole parsed track; there is no chunked path natively to switch.
OctopusOptions.prescaleFactor: An internal canvas scale ratio the WASM wrapper uses to trade sharpness for CPU. AssRenderer has no such knob — frameSize()/storageSize() are the only sizing surface, and libass renders at the requested size directly.
OctopusOptions.renderAhead: How many frames the WASM wrapper pre-computes ahead of currentTime, its own buffering strategy. AssRenderer.render(timeMillis) is a synchronous per-frame call with no lookahead cache to configure.
OctopusOptions.renderMode: Chooses between a `js` and a `wasm` libass backend in the browser. The port links one native libass binding; there is no second backend to choose between.
OctopusOptions.targetFps: Paces the WASM wrapper's own render loop. AssRenderer.render() is driven by the video's frame callback; the port has no independent render loop to pace.
OctopusOptions.workerUrl: The URL of the JS Worker script the browser's renderer runs in. The port calls libass directly, off no worker.
OctopusPlugin.initialize: The web Plugin base's lifecycle hook, overridden to merge options before the kit's own call. The native base spells this use() and every plugin already has it.
SpectrumPlugin.analyser: Returns an AnalyserNode. Native frames arrive through the graph's tap.
addClasses: DOM class manipulation on the mount element. Compose has no class list; the native chrome styles itself with modifiers.
audioContext: The Web Audio AudioContext the browser hands out. Native audio processing goes through the AudioDspGraph port, which is a different object with a different lifetime, not this one renamed.
container: The HTMLElement the web player mounts into. A native player is handed a surface through the video backend port rather than owning a view.
createButton: Builds a chrome button element. The native chrome composes its own controls.
createElement: Builds an HTMLElement for the web chrome. The native chrome is composed, not constructed.
createSVG: Builds an SVG node for the web chrome. The native chrome draws vectors through its own toolkit.
experimental: A runtime override table that swaps player methods by string key. Kotlin has no prototype to patch and no string-keyed method table, so the surface cannot exist; a native consumer overrides by subclassing an open member.
removeClasses: DOM class manipulation on the mount element. Compose has no class list; the native chrome styles itself with modifiers.
selectAudioOutput: The browser's own output-device picker (navigator.mediaDevices.selectAudioOutput, Chrome only). No native platform offers a picker to open; routing to a known device is audioOutput(id).
videoElement: The HTMLVideoElement the web player drives. The native equivalent is the backend's surface, which the port exposes rather than the player.
